visual: Broad glossy leathery leaves variegated dark green, cream and pink, with pink midribs and margins; new leaves the most vividly coloured · upright single stem
water: Water when the top of the compost dries; less in winter
soilWarning: Bright indirect light keeps the pink
prune: Prune in spring to control height; cut stems bleed white sap
toxicity: Milky sap is harmful if eaten and may irritate skin and eyes
hardinessNote: RHS H1b; indoors or under glass, roughly 10-15°C minimum
resilience: Variegated leaves scorch in direct sun and fade to green in poor light; otherwise as tough as the plain species
uncertain: PROVENANCE: derived by Claude on 2026-09-27 from the deck's held Ficus elastica card (itself written by Claude, not the research pipeline) plus retail descriptions of 'Belize' (Thompson & Morgan, Proven Winners). Not checked against RHS or Kew.
Only visual, hue, cvs, soilWarning and resilience differ from the species card; every rating is carried over unchanged and is an editorial judgement, not researched.
Height and spread are INDOOR container figures; T&M quotes an eventual 3 m x 1.5 m.
